title: Professional development: action research on in-service teacher education for those who teach Mathematics
text_snippet: Professional development: action research on in-service teacher education for those who teach Mathematics The study sought to identify and understand interactive processes and constitutive elements of the professional development of teachers who teach Mathematics, emerging from collaborative in-service teacher education. Grounded in Vygotsky’s socio-interactionist perspective, in the criteria for effective professional development, and in learning communities, the study was conducted as qualitative action research with five teachers from a public school. Data were produced through field diaries, audio recordings, and teachers’ written productions and organized into dialogical interactive episodes. The results indicate a shift from individual to collaborative planning, the development of tasks with pedagogical intentionality, and the adoption of an investigative stance toward students’ reasoning. It is concluded that the school and peer interaction constitute important conditions for reflective practices and teachers’ professional development.

title: The Theory of Mathematics in the Context of Sciences and its theoretical-methodological potential when articulated with other frameworks
text_snippet: The Theory of Mathematics in the Context of Sciences and its theoretical-methodological potential when articulated with other frameworks This study analyzes the theoretical-methodological potential arising from the articulation of the Theory of Mathematics in the Context of Sciences with other frameworks in Mathematics Education, focusing on teaching and learning in Engineering programs. This qualitative, bibliographic investigation is based on the analysis of studies conducted by the authors, in which TMCC is articulated with the Anthropological Theory of the Didactic, the Theory of Structural Cognitive Modifiability, the Theory of Conceptual Fields, and the Theory of Semiotic Representation Registers. The results show that these articulations enhance the analytical and propositional power of the investigations, enabling the construction of a more robust theoretical-methodological structure and supporting more consistent teaching practices in extra-mathematical contexts.

title: Mathematics is not neutral: teachers’ conceptions of antiracist education in quilombola communities
text_snippet: Mathematics is not neutral: teachers’ conceptions of antiracist education in quilombola communities This qualitative study aimed to identify the conceptions of teachers who teach Mathematics in schools located in quilombola communities in the municipality of Senhor do Bonfim, Brazil, regarding educational policies addressing ethnic-racial relations. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire, enabling an analysis of teachers' understandings of the current legislation and its implications for Mathematics teaching. The findings indicate that, despite gaps in initial teacher education concerning anti-racist education, teachers recognize the relevance of these policies and identify possibilities for connecting Mathematics teaching with the appreciation of Black culture. The study also reveals teachers' insecurity in addressing racial issues, as well as the positive impact of these practices on students' critical thinking, self-esteem, and sense of belonging.

title: Pedagogical Residency Program: reflections on its contributions to initial teacher education
text_snippet: Pedagogical Residency Program: reflections on its contributions to initial teacher education This study aimed to analyze the contribution of the Pedagogical Residency Program at Unimontes, Mathematics subproject, to the initial education of its graduates, investigating the extent to which the Program has fostered the development of the knowledge, skills, and competencies required for high-quality teaching in Basic Education. Methodologically, a questionnaire comprising open and closed-ended questions was administered to 44 residents in the subproject. The findings indicate that the Program played a significant role in initial teacher education by providing both theoretical and practical foundations for teaching practice, as well as by contributing to licentiate students' retention in the undergraduate program and strengthening their professional identity.

title: Didactic-Mathematical Knowledge in the initial education of Mathematics teachers: an analysis within the context of the Pedagogical Residency Program
text_snippet: Didactic-Mathematical Knowledge in the initial education of Mathematics teachers: an analysis within the context of the Pedagogical Residency Program This study analyzed the reflections of pre-service Mathematics teachers regarding the learning opportunities provided by the Pedagogical Residency Program, focusing on the development of the knowledge required for teaching. The theoretical framework is grounded in the Didactic-Mathematical Knowledge model. The study is qualitative in nature, adopting an interpretive approach, with data generated through questionnaires and semi-structured interviews and analyzed using Content Analysis. The analysis is organized into two categories corresponding to the ecological and interactional facets. The findings indicate that the practices developed by the pre-service teachers foster reflective processes about teaching and contribute to the development of professional knowledge. It is concluded that the Pedagogical Residency Program constitutes a formative space for the construction of teaching knowledge, even in challenging contexts.

title: The Geometry and the Mathematical Knowledge Specific to Teaching in Mathematics Teacher Education Programs in Paraíba La Geometría y el Conocimiento Matemático Propio de la Docencia en las Licenciaturas en Matemáticas de Paraíba
text_snippet: The Geometry and the Mathematical Knowledge Specific to Teaching in Mathematics Teacher Education Programs in Paraíba La Geometría y el Conocimiento Matemático Propio de la Docencia en las Licenciaturas en Matemáticas de Paraíba The education of Mathematics teachers reveals tensions between academic knowledge and the demands of Basic Education, especially in the teaching of Geometry. This study aimed to understand how Geometry is addressed in Mathematics teacher education programs at public institutions in Paraíba, Brazil, based on the analysis of Pedagogical Course Projects, with emphasis on course syllabi. This is a qualitative, documentary, exploratory-descriptive study. The results indicate the predominance of Academic Mathematics, with limited articulation with teaching and with Mathematical Knowledge Specific to Teaching. Gaps in initial teacher education are evident, particularly regarding the integration of content, pedagogical practice, and school demands, pointing to the need for curricula that foster the development of professional teaching knowledge.

title: Between points and knowledges: tensions between school knowledge and traditional knowledge in quilombola handicrafts
text_snippet: Between points and knowledges: tensions between school knowledge and traditional knowledge in quilombola handicrafts This study sought to discuss and identify how quilombola practices and forms of knowledge articulate mathematical knowledge, highlighting the tensions between hegemonic school knowledge and traditional knowledge involved in grass handling. Grounded in discourse analysis, the study examines 36 events involving women and adolescent craftswomen from the Raiz quilombo, located in the municipality of Presidente Kubitschek, in the Espinhaço Mountain Range, Minas Gerais, Brazil. The research involved three participants (women, men, and adolescents) and employed Oral History as a methodological approach, in addition to the observation of everyday activities related to handicrafts. The findings reveal the need to value these local forms of knowledge which, although often marginalized within formal education, hold significant cultural and pedagogical meaning.

title: A Discursive Textual Analysis on Mathematics teaching in light of the Pedagogical Principles of Rural Education
text_snippet: A Discursive Textual Analysis on Mathematics teaching in light of the Pedagogical Principles of Rural Education This article is an excerpt from a dissertation that aimed to analyze the perceptions of educators who teach mathematics in rural schools in the municipality of Parauapebas, Brazil, regarding the Pedagogical Principles of Rural Education. The research is qualitative in nature; we initially investigated educational documents focused on rural education, followed by semi-structured interviews with teachers. We used Discursive Textual Analysis to analyze the interview data. The results revealed that rural educators recognize the importance of contextualizing mathematics content in the classroom and value the local knowledge, experiences, and insights of rural communities.

title: The Guardian of Life Game: knowledge of babassu coconut breakers, Ethnomathematics, and Youth, Adult, and Elderly Education
text_snippet: The Guardian of Life Game: knowledge of babassu coconut breakers, Ethnomathematics, and Youth, Adult, and Elderly Education The study aimed to unveil the possibilities of the Capemba Guardian of Life game for the teaching of Mathematics in the Youth, Adult, and Elderly Education modality (EJAI). The theoretical foundation is anchored in the Ethnomathematics Program, whose principal interlocutors in the dialogue are Ubiratan D’Ambrosio, Ubiratan D’Ambrosio Vergani, Vizolli, Barros, and Fialho, through a qualitative approach. The results reveal that the game constitutes a transdisciplinary pedagogical resource for the teaching of Mathematics in the EJAI modality by mobilizing knowledge related to the place value of numbers. It is concluded that the learning of school Mathematics in EJAI can be enhanced by taking as a reference the sociocultural knowledge and practices of babassu coconut breakers in the Cocais Region, in Maranhão, Brazil.

title: Ethnomodelling research at GEPTEMaC: paths and reflections of a scientific collective
text_snippet: Ethnomodelling research at GEPTEMaC: paths and reflections of a scientific collective The research reported in this article presents the Study and Research Group on Trends in Mathematics Education and Culture (GEPTEMaC), highlighting its role in Mathematics Education through the analysis of ongoing and ongoing Ethnomodeling investigations. The theoretical and methodological paths taken, the collective reflections, and the contributions to the dialogue between culture and mathematics are highlighted. Qualitative and theoretical in nature, the investigation adopted the methodological procedure of analyzing 21 academic productions — at the undergraduate, master's, and doctoral levels — examined using the Content Analysis technique. The results point to Ethnomodeling as a possibility that values ​​culture in studies, recognizing mathematical knowledge and practices in sociocultural environments. GEPTEMaC has strengthened the academic debate and expanded its national reach.

title: When Ethnomathematics meets Gert Biesta: possible dialogues and productive tensions
text_snippet: When Ethnomathematics meets Gert Biesta: possible dialogues and productive tensions The research aimed to discuss the dialogue between theoretical contributions from the field of Ethnomathematics and some produced by the educator Gert Biesta, especially those expressed in his work The (Re)discovery of Teaching. With regard to Ethnomathematics, the perspective adopted is that of Gelsa Knijnik, intersecting ideas from Ludwig Wittgenstein's mature work and a set of Foucauldian notions. The results point to the productivity of the dialogues, since the similarities are expressed in three important pillars when considering teaching and learning processes: criticism of learning measurement processes, problematization of scientific advances, and the role of teachers in teaching processes.

title: Between files and pedagogical practices: the legacy of Ubiratan D’Ambrosio on the Assessment-Report
text_snippet: Between files and pedagogical practices: the legacy of Ubiratan D’Ambrosio on the Assessment-Report A dialogue is established based on the results of two studies on the Assessment-Report, a model conceived by Ubiratan D’Ambrosio. The first study consists of a postdoctoral research in the Postgraduate Program in Science and Mathematics Education at the Federal University of Uberlândia, and the other in a training workshop involving documents from the Ubiratan D’Ambrosio Personal Archive (APUA). In addition to the aim is sharing investigative and training activities with documents from the aforementioned archive, to contribute to reflections on emancipatory assessment practices in Mathematics Education. In the documentary research at APUA and in the analysis of graduate students' narratives, the Assessment-Report reveals itself as an emancipatory practice that interfaces with the dimensions of the Ethnomathematics Program, respecting the cultural roots of the student and promoting their critical autonomy.

title: The process of disciplinarization of Descriptive Geometry in Brazil in the 19th and 20th centuries
text_snippet: The process of disciplinarization of Descriptive Geometry in Brazil in the 19th and 20th centuries The process of disciplinarization of Descriptive Geometry in Brazil is directly related to the creation of the Royal Military Academy of Rio de Janeiro in the early 19th century. Greatly inspired by the École Polytechnique de Paris and created in 1810, the Military Academy introduced Descriptive Geometry as part of its program. This research aimed to analyze the process of disciplinarization of Descriptive Geometry in Brazil in the 19th and 20th centuries, using a qualitative approach based on textual and contextual analysis. The analysis indicated that the process of disciplinarization of Descriptive Geometry in Brazil was characterized, from the outset, as a repetition of methods, created solely as a teaching discipline and not for research.

title: The Boi Pintadinho Festival and School Mathematics Education: a dialogue between colors and knowledge
text_snippet: The Boi Pintadinho Festival and School Mathematics Education: a dialogue between colors and knowledge Originating from professional master's research, this paper focuses on the cultural practices of Boi Pintadinho in Muqui, Brazil, and its connection with school mathematics education. The investigation adopts an ethnomathematical perspective, based on D'Ambrosio and Bishop, conceiving mathematics as a human and cultural construction. The text reports on a pilot experiment with a qualitative and ethnographic approach, carried out through participant observation in 2024, recording forms, rhythms, and choreographies. The analysis followed Bishop's activities: counting, measuring, locating, projecting, playing, and explaining. The findings reveal practices intertwined with these processes, integrating cultural knowledge and school mathematical thinking. It is concluded that the ethnomathematical approach offers paths to diversified education and contextualized learning.

title: Making a box for honey production: conversations with a rural producer
text_snippet: Making a box for honey production: conversations with a rural producer The theme of this article is the construction of wooden boxes intended for honey production by bees. These boxes are located on the rural property of a small producer in Córrego Central, in the community of Cristalino, municipality of Nova Venécia, Espírito Santo. The objective of the research was to investigate the mathematization strategies of small farmers in the construction of beehives. It is found that the construction of beehives can be used as a didactic resource to assist in the teaching and learning of mathematical concepts of plane and spatial geometry. It is concluded that the mathematical practice of the rural producer acts as a subsidy for students to produce knowledge, through the articulation between concrete and abstract thinking, within the scope of geometric concepts.

title: Ethnomathematics and Architecture: the historic buildings of UFRRJ as a resource for teaching Mathematics
text_snippet: Ethnomathematics and Architecture: the historic buildings of UFRRJ as a resource for teaching Mathematics This study investigated the presence of Ethnomathematics in the buildings of the Federal Rural University of Rio de Janeiro, seeking to understand how architectural elements reveal mathematical practices in cultural and historical contexts. The objective was to analyze how the observation and interpretation of buildings can support pedagogical practices that make mathematics teaching more sensitive to cultural diversity. The research combines a literature review, relating Ethnomathematics, Architecture, and the history of the institution, with visual and structural analysis, considering geometric aspects and constructive solutions. The results indicate that architecture transcends its functional and ornamental character, incorporating mathematical manifestations with cultural value, highlighting its potential as a teaching resource, bringing it closer to students' daily lives.

title: Unit of measurement fathom: ethnomathematics, teaching and learning
text_snippet: Unit of measurement fathom: ethnomathematics, teaching and learning Historically created measurement systems have been preserved by sociocultural groups that continue to use ancestral measures, such as the hectare, the tarefa (units of area measurement), and the fathom (a unit of length measurement), in their daily activities. The objective of the research was to reflect on units of measurement that are cultural heritages as possibilities for teaching and learning mathematical concepts. The theoretical framework draws on authors in ethnomathematics and ancestral measurement; the methodological approach adopted was qualitative ethnographic research. The results show that cultural dynamics can be a strategy for teaching and learning in the ways of mathematizing the environment. It is concluded that this knowledge and these practices in the classroom are one of the ways to challenge the status quo established in an imposed curriculum.

title: Ethnomathematics, displacements, and borders: a study with Haitians in São Paulo
text_snippet: Ethnomathematics, displacements, and borders: a study with Haitians in São Paulo This article presents the results of doctoral research on intercultural education, grounded in Ubiratan D’Ambrosio’s Ethnomathematics Program in dialogue with Paulo Freire. The research aimed to analyze the connections between education and politics in the context of Haitian immigrants’ schooling. To this end, the methodology of being in borders was developed, based on processes of otherness, listening, and dialogue. The research took place in two stages: participant observation at a Youth and Adult Education Center (CIEJA) in São Paulo, Brazil, and interviews with the principal, three teachers, and two Haitian students. The results highlight the relationships established within the school community and point to three boundaries that shape immigrants’ trajectories: racism, professional training, and language.

title: Ethnomathematics and Enawenê-Nawê Culture: the processes of generation, updating, and dissemination of knowledge in the rituals at Iyaõkwa Hakolone
text_snippet: Ethnomathematics and Enawenê-Nawê Culture: the processes of generation, updating, and dissemination of knowledge in the rituals at Iyaõkwa Hakolone This research analyzed the processes of construction of the Iyaõkwa Hakolone ritual house of the Enawenê-Nawê people from the perspective of Ethnomathematics, seeking to understand how mathematical knowledge emerges in these stages. Data were collected through focus group interviews with leaders, teachers, and guardians of tradition, aiming to identify cultural, aesthetic, and mathematical meanings associated with the ritual house. The results indicate that the construction integrates cosmological principles, material resistance, and geometric organization, forming a sacred space of cultural convergence. It is concluded that the Iyaõkwa Hakolone represents a microcosm of the Enawenê-Nawê worldview, highlighting the union between traditional knowledge, social identity, and spirituality.

title: Ethnography and the (re)construction of differences: (mis)steps towards a possible Anthropology of Mathematics Education
text_snippet: Ethnography and the (re)construction of differences: (mis)steps towards a possible Anthropology of Mathematics Education This research aimed to explore how debates on ethnography can provide analytical insights for understanding the processes of teaching and learning Mathematics in different sociocultural contexts, taking it as the central axis of this approach. Thus, a debate is held on the concept(s) of ethnography(ies) based on contemporary authors in Anthropology, as well as on how this concept has been (re)signified and (re)interpreted in the anthropological discipline itself, which makes it possible to understand its role in the construction of differences and in the relationship with otherness(es). Understanding this context is fundamental to proposing an Anthropology of Mathematics Education, because the way in which otherness is dealt with and written about is central to the processes of teaching and learning Mathematics.

title: Methodological approach to division: a reflection in light of Angolan Elementary School Mathematics textbooks and the experiences of three teachers
text_snippet: Methodological approach to division: a reflection in light of Angolan Elementary School Mathematics textbooks and the experiences of three teachers This study examined how the division operation is presented in elementary Mathematics textbooks in Angola and how it is taught by teachers. Methodologically, it involved analyzing content and tasks from textbooks for grades 1 to 6, as well as interviews with three teachers. The findings indicate that both textbooks and teaching practices emphasize low-demand tasks focused on mastering the division algorithm. This approach limits conceptual understanding, reducing division to the execution of calculations and procedural rules. The study also identified the absence of tasks that explore the meanings of ratio and combination. It concludes that division is approached in a restricted manner, which hinders the development of meaningful learning and students’ progression to more advanced levels of mathematical understanding.

title: Mathematics education for peace: from micro to macro
text_snippet: Mathematics education for peace: from micro to macro The research in this theoretical essay proposes an understanding of mathematics education for peace in the micro and macro dimensions, relating it to understandings of microviolence and macroviolence inside and outside the classroom. For this purpose, national literature was consulted. It is argued that this education requires continuous vigilance over the (re)production and (trans)formation of violence, with a view to rejecting it. These forms of violence are understood in the historical, social, and political contexts of a given era and understood as an open field. It also defends the existence of an open transition between micro and macro violence in mathematics education, experienced in a unique way by individuals.

title: The Pedagogical Residency Program and teacher education from the perspective of preceptors in the Mathematics subprojects at UFSJ
text_snippet: The Pedagogical Residency Program and teacher education from the perspective of preceptors in the Mathematics subprojects at UFSJ This paper is part of the Pedagogical Residency Program linked to the Licentiate Degree in Mathematics course at the Federal University of São João del-Rei (PRP-Mat at UFSJ), focusing on preceptors. The research aims to understand, based on their voices, the contributions of PRP-Mat at UFSJ to the education of mathematics teachers, residents and preceptors. Three mathematics teachers who served as preceptors in subprojects of the PRP-Mat at UFSJ participated in this qualitative research, which was an instrumental case study. The results indicate that the hybrid configuration makes the Pedagogical Residency Program conducive to the creation of a third space for the education of mathematics teachers, not only for initial teacher education, but also for preceptors.

title: Written Text Production in the education of teachers who teach Mathematics: a state of knowledge
text_snippet: Written Text Production in the education of teachers who teach Mathematics: a state of knowledge This article presents a state of knowledge study on written textual production in the education of teachers who teach Mathematics. The aim of this study was to analyze how written textual production has been conceptualized, mobilized, and problematized in Brazilian theses and dissertations. The study is characterized as qualitative, bibliographic in design, taking as its corpus academic works defended between 2006 and 2024 and retrieved from publicly accessible digital databases. The analysis is grounded in sociointeractionist perspectives of language and in the conception of Mathematics as a form of discourse. The results indicate that written textual production assumes different educative statuses — ranging from a didactic resource to a practice of professional development and reflective/narrative writing of teaching —, yet remains weakly institutionalized, revealing the absence of its consolidation as a structuring dimension of Mathematics teacher education.

title: The development of Computational Thinking in mathematical proofs
text_snippet: The development of Computational Thinking in mathematical proofs This paper presents research that aimed to show the possibilities for developing Computational Thinking (CT) in various types of Mathematical Proofs (MP). Using a qualitative research approach, a set of MP was selected, identifying in each of them the practices and processes associated with CT that can be mobilized in each proof. The research conclusions highlight that the articulation between CT and MP favors the understanding of formal notions such as generalization, logical rigor, and argumentative validity, which are fundamental in the teaching and learning processes of Mathematics. This articulation also contributes to the development of systematic, abstract forms of reasoning that can be transferred to different mathematical contexts.

title: Potential of the Pedagogical Residency Program in the education of Mathematics teachers at the Federal University of Uberlândia
text_snippet: Potential of the Pedagogical Residency Program in the education of Mathematics teachers at the Federal University of Uberlândia This paper discusses the potential of the Pedagogical Residency Program (PRP) in the education of Mathematics teachers. The analysis, based on the assumptions of paradigmatic analysis, used reports from residents of the Mathematics course at the Federal University of Uberlândia (UFU), Santa Monica campus, linked to the Interdisciplinary Center for Physics and Mathematics, during eighteen months of the third PRP call for applications. The results indicate that, among other potentialities, the problematization of the theme of assessment proved to be important, leading to the recognition of its formative relevance. In this sense, the PRP contributed to the constitution of an unprecedented-viable: the possible creation of a curriculum component focused on the study of assessment in the Licentiate Degree in Mathematics at UFU.

title: World hunger from the perspective of members of the Pedagogical Residency Program: contributions from Critical Mathematics Education
text_snippet: World hunger from the perspective of members of the Pedagogical Residency Program: contributions from Critical Mathematics Education The qualitative study whose objective is to identify, from the perspective of the advisor and the preceptor of a Pedagogical Residency Program, dialogues between a project developed with sixth-grade classes in a public school, focused on the theme of world hunger, and the principles of Critical Mathematics Education (CME). The stages of the project were analyzed in light of discussions in CME, which seeks to train students to develop a critical view of the society in which they live and to think about possibilities for transforming it. This process gave rise to some significant dialogues between the project and CME, especially those related to the exploration of Mathematics beyond calculation, the type of communication established in Mathematics classes, and the practices of reading and writing about the world mediated by Mathematics.

title: Pedagogical Residency Program: education of educators
text_snippet: Pedagogical Residency Program: education of educators This research is descriptive in nature, qualitative in approach, and part of a project conceived and developed collaboratively by a network of researchers from Minas Gerais, Brazil, who are dedicated to researching the Pedagogical Residency Program. The research focused on the education of educators, considering both the advisor and the preceptor as co-trainers of the residents, seeking to understand the contributions of participation in the Program to the education of Mathematics educators teacher. Data from questionnaires answered by the preceptors were analyzed. These data enable reflection on the experiences of Higher Education Institutions in Minas Gerais and point to practices that have proven successful in the process of immersing future teachers in the school context.

title: A reading on the development of the three editions of the Pedagogical Residency Program from the perspective of a professor educator
text_snippet: A reading on the development of the three editions of the Pedagogical Residency Program from the perspective of a professor educator The objective of the study was to analyze the three editions of the development of subprojects of the Pedagogical Residency Program (PRP) at the Federal University of Alfenas, focusing on the education aspect of students and the education professor who advisor the Licentiate Degree in Mathematics. To this end, an analysis of the professor educator's actions and notes was carried out, based on the assumptions of the Model of Semantic Fields, in particular plausible reading. Each edition of the PRP contributed to the education of the teacher education by enabling deep immersion in schools, bringing them closer to professional practice and also to the advisor who made changes to the subprojects in light of previous experiences, constantly (re)thinking the orientation process.

title: Contributions of Mathematical Modeling to the mobilization of mathematical content in a 7th grade Middle School class
text_snippet: Contributions of Mathematical Modeling to the mobilization of mathematical content in a 7th grade Middle School class This paper is part of a dissertation that developed Mathematical Modeling practices in the classroom and on a walking track, using the structure of a Mathematical Modeling Cycle as a theoretical reference. The research sought to answer: what are the contributions of Mathematical Modeling in a 7th grade Middle School class to the mobilization of mathematical content and the development of mathematical and social skills? The research analyzed how the mobilization of mathematical content occurred, highlighting the potential of the approach. The methodology proved effective in expanding content development, achieving skills at subsequent levels, and improving essential skills for citizenship training.

title: Analysis of teaching learning mobilized by residents in the Pedagogical Residency Program in Mathematics
text_snippet: Analysis of teaching learning mobilized by residents in the Pedagogical Residency Program in Mathematics The objective of the research reported in this paper was to analyze the learning revealed by graduates of the Pedagogical Residency Program (PRP) in Minas Gerais, Brazil, as they reflected on their participation in Mathematics subprojects. To this end, the assumptions of Social Learning Theory were used. This is a qualitative study with 102 residents who responded to a semi-structured questionnaire. The data was organized into four categories, involving learning as belonging, as doing, as experience, and as transformation. The results indicate a sense of belonging, the development of projects and activities related to teaching practice, and the creation of education spaces. It is concluded that the PRP has established itself as a place for teacher education by promoting integration into the school context, dialogue, and the collective construction of knowledge.

title: Práctica pedagógica de la Matemática: saberes contextualizados en la decolonialidad planetaria-complejidad
text_snippet: Práctica pedagógica de la Matemática: saberes contextualizados en la decolonialidad planetaria-complejidad El objetivo del ensayo fue analizar la práctica pedagógica de la Matemática: saberes contextualizados en la decolonialidad planetaria-complejidad. Para ello usamos las transmetodologías decoloniales planetaria complejas, con el transmétodo la hermenéutica comprensiva ecosófica y diatópica pasando por los momentos analíticos, empíricos y propositivos. En el momento analítico-empírico estudiamos consultando a autores originales de las categorías de estudio la práctica pedagógica de la Matemática en la tradicionalidad modernista-postmodernista. En los momentos propositivos nos desprendemos de la cita de autores y vamos a concretar el objetivo de estudio con la práctica pedagógica de la Matemática — saberes contextualizados en la decolonialidad planetaria-complejidad y las conclusiones no definitivas.

title: A look at non-Euclidean Geometries in Basic Education
text_snippet: A look at non-Euclidean Geometries in Basic Education The research presented in this article analyzed a teacher's reflective narrative on teaching non-Euclidean Geometries in Basic Education. Her experience is tied to her practice in schools, teacher education, and engagement with Mathematics Education. Qualitative analysis of the narrative showed that the inclusion of this content can broaden understanding of geometry, promote interdisciplinary connections, and contribute to citizenship education. However, challenges are highlighted, such as the scarcity of this content in textbooks, school curriculum, and Mathematics teacher’s education, as well as tensions between Euclidean and non-Euclidean concepts. It is concluded that working with this content in Basic Education can stimulate critical thinking, creativity, and the view of Mathematics as a human construct.

title: Creencias del profesor sobre material bibliográfico para enseñar Matemáticas en Educación Media Superior
text_snippet: Creencias del profesor sobre material bibliográfico para enseñar Matemáticas en Educación Media Superior El objetivo del estudio fue identificar las creencias de dos profesoras acerca del material curricular bibliográfico para la enseñanza de las Matemáticas en Educación Media Superior. Para ello, se llevó a cabo un estudio descriptivo, con un enfoque cualitativo, configurado como un estudio de caso. Los dados fueron producidos mediante entrevista semiestructurada y posteriormente analizados a partir de dos categorías emergentes: criterios para la utilización del material bibliográfico y criterios para la selección de dicho material. Los resultados muestran que las creencias de ambos profesores están relacionadas con la percepción que tienen sobre cómo aprenden sus estudiantes, tomando como referencia las normativas de la institución en la que trabajan y las experiencias vividas por los profesores en su trayectoria como estudiantes.

title: Graph of an affine function: a study from the perspective of the Potential Didactic Contract
text_snippet: Graph of an affine function: a study from the perspective of the Potential Didactic Contract The research aimed to investigate the potential didactic contract through expectations, potential contract rules, and indications of rupture present in a 1st-grade High School Mathematics textbook regarding the knowledge of the graph of the affine function. The technique adopted was document analysis, taking as a reference the definition of the elements that compose this contract. A total of three expectations, one potential explicit rule, three potential implicit rules, and two indications of rupture were identified. The results point to regularities that show a tendency towards standardization of the procedures for constructing the graph of the affine function, revealing both the strength of these regularities and their possible limits for the production of broader mathematical meanings.

title: Mathematical tasks on Probability in 6th-grade Middle School textbooks approved by the PNLD 2024
text_snippet: Mathematical tasks on Probability in 6th-grade Middle School textbooks approved by the PNLD 2024 Mathematical tasks (TM) are present in teaching materials and are widely used by teachers. They come in various types and serve different purposes during class. The study aimed to understand the role of TM proposed by textbooks (LD) for teaching Probability in the 6th grade of Middle School, as approved by the PNLD 2024. Using a qualitative approach, thirteen collections were examined, identifying the number of TM on Probability and analyzing the potential (or lack thereof) of some of them. The results reveal the predominance of TM with low cognitive demand, with a scarce presence of open proposals and an absence of investigative TM. The analysis highlights conceptual and methodological gaps that limit the development of students' probabilistic literacy. As a result, there is a need to reconfigure the tasks in the textbooks, with greater emphasis on contextualized and investigative proposals.

title: Deaf teacher, inclusive practices, and ethnomathematical perspectives in the regular classroom Docentes sordos, prácticas inclusivas y perspectivas etnomatemáticas en la educación regular
text_snippet: Deaf teacher, inclusive practices, and ethnomathematical perspectives in the regular classroom Docentes sordos, prácticas inclusivas y perspectivas etnomatemáticas en la educación regular This paper presents the results of a study that aimed to examine the presence of a deaf teacher in regular classes in the Elementary School. Using Ethnomathematics as a theoretical and methodological reference, data were generated from a study group comprising hearing and deaf teachers who worked with deaf students in two public schools in municipalities in Mato Grosso, Brazil. The participants designed, developed, evaluated, and redesigned tasks using GeoGebra as an assistive technology. The analysis showed that deaf teachers can work in regular classrooms, provided they have the support of a professional Brazilian Sign Language (Libras) translator-interpreter.

title: Calculation strategies of sugarcane workers regarding their work journeys Estrategias del cálculo de los trabajadores cañeros sobre sus jornadas laborales
text_snippet: Calculation strategies of sugarcane workers regarding their work journeys Estrategias del cálculo de los trabajadores cañeros sobre sus jornadas laborales This study analyzed the strategies used by a sugarcane worker to determine the remuneration of a sugarcane cutter, considering his roles as cutter, overseer, and inspector. The objective was to understand and explain his perceptions through cell phone-recorded interviews about his professional trajectory, which characterizes a qualitative case study. As a result, the adoption of unusual methods was observed, such as transforming triangles into rectangles and decomposing the area of ​​land with elevations, without resorting to procedures taught in school. The interaction between the overseer, the inspector, and the cutters in measuring the areas reveals conflicts related to benefits and losses, demonstrating an awareness of the need to avoid social injustices.

title: A teaching sequence for the development of statistical literacy in the 1st grade Elementary School
text_snippet: A teaching sequence for the development of statistical literacy in the 1st grade Elementary School With this study, an analysis was conducted on the teaching of Statistics in the 1st grade of Elementary School, considering its contribution to scientific thinking. Of a qualitative nature and with a theoretical-propositional character, the study is supported by a recent bibliographic review on statistical literacy in Elementary School and by references from the field. It presents a teaching sequence, which is analyzed based on the theoretical framework, articulating the cognitive and attitudinal components of statistical literacy and the use of concrete materials. Its main objective was to analyze the potentialities and limitations of the teaching sequence, offering contributions that provide support for future research and for teaching practice in statistics education.

title: Fruit production in the Matapi Agricultural Colony and Ethnomathematics: contributions and frontiers La producción frutícola en la Colonia Agrícola Matapi y la Etnomatemática: aportes y fronteras
text_snippet: Fruit production in the Matapi Agricultural Colony and Ethnomathematics: contributions and frontiers La producción frutícola en la Colonia Agrícola Matapi y la Etnomatemática: aportes y fronteras The research aimed to analyze fruit production as a sustainability strategy in knowledge/practice and survival in the Matapi Agricultural Colony. Using a qualitative approach and ethnographic research, techniques such as participant observation and group discussions were used. Reference is made to the studies of D’Ambrosio (2011, 2020), Mattos (2015), Mattos (2020), Mesquita (2023), among others. The narratives of Mrs. Raimundinha and her son are presented in the discussions and results, addressing the concept of Ethnomathematics in approaches with the dimensions formulated by D'Ambrosio (2011) and the affective dimension created by Mattos (2020). It is concluded that pineapple production enables dialogue and exchange between local beings, knowledge, and practices, as well as some school mathematical concepts.
